title: Durvalumab + gemcitabine + cisplatin
context_label: Unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer
schedule_summary: Cycles 1–8 at most: day 1 all three infusions; day 8 gemcitabine and cisplatin only. Each cycle lasts 21 days. From cycle 9, if continuing: durvalumab alone every 28 days.
purpose: First-line treatment to slow advanced bile duct or gallbladder cancer and help people live longer.
indication_text: Unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer
administration_text: Cycles 1–8 at most: day 1 all three infusions; day 8 gemcitabine and cisplatin only. Each cycle lasts 21 days. From cycle 9, if continuing: durvalumab alone every 28 days.
monitoring_summary: Before starting: blood count, kidney and liver profile, glucose and thyroid function. Hearing assessment if indicated. During treatment: day 1 full blood count, kidney and liver checks; during chemotherapy day 8 full blood count and creatinine; regular glucose and thyroid tests, with cortisol if clinically indicated.
review_status: Feasibility build. Clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Durvalumab
agents.explanation: Blocks a signal called PD-L1 that some cancers use to switch off immune cells. This can help immune cells recognise and attack cancer.
agents.mechanism: Blocks a signal called PD-L1 that some cancers use to switch off immune cells. This can help immune cells recognise and attack cancer.
visual: Blocks a signal called PD-L1 that some cancers use to switch off immune cells. This can help immune cells recognise and attack cancer.
agents.watch: Immune cells can inflame healthy organs, including after the final infusion. Carry your immunotherapy alert card.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Resembles a building block for DNA. It interferes with making new DNA in dividing cells.
agents.mechanism: Resembles a building block for DNA. It interferes with making new DNA in dividing cells.
visual: Resembles a building block for DNA. It interferes with making new DNA in dividing cells.
agents.watch: Low blood counts can increase the risk of infection, bruising and bleeding.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Links strands of DNA together, making it difficult for dividing cancer cells to copy their instructions.
agents.mechanism: Links strands of DNA together, making it difficult for dividing cancer cells to copy their instructions.
visual: Links strands of DNA together, making it difficult for dividing cancer cells to copy their instructions.
agents.watch: Tell the team about reduced urine, ringing in the ears, hearing loss or tingling.

anatomy: New cough or breathlessness: call oncology urgently.
Marked weakness, dizziness or severe headache: call urgently.
Yellow eyes, dark urine or upper abdominal pain: call urgently.
New diarrhoea, blood in stools or tummy pain: call urgently.
Much less urine or swelling: phone the team.
Report ringing, muffled hearing or a change in hearing.
Fever, shaking or suddenly feeling unwell: call immediately.
Report new tingling, numbness or problems walking.
anatomy_note: Numbers link each body location to an action. Effects can have several causes and can arise after the last immunotherapy dose.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests before and during treatment

rows.label: Before
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver function, glucose and thyroid function
Baseline results help the team recognise changes.

rows.label: Before, if needed
cells: Your team may refer you if hearing or tinnitus is a concern.

rows.label: During treatment
cells: Day 1: blood count, kidney and liver tests. Day 8 in the chemotherapy phase: blood count and creatinine.
Cisplatin can injure the kidneys. Your team checks results before giving treatment.

rows.label: During treatment
cells: Glucose and thyroid function regularly; cortisol if clinically indicated.
New weakness, dizziness or vomiting may prompt hormone tests.

rows.label: Local plan
cells: Your unit may request additional tests, such as hepatitis screening, depending on its policy or your history.
The Irish biliary protocol does not specify routine hepatitis testing or mandatory PD-L1 tumour testing.

monitoring_schedule.note: Follow the dates supplied by your hospital.

urgent_extra: Fever, shaking chills or jaundice may signal serious infection, especially with a bile duct stent. Contact oncology immediately. New cough, breathlessness or diarrhoea is also urgent.

sections.title: Your first visit
sections.text: On day 1 you receive durvalumab, gemcitabine and cisplatin. On day 8 you receive gemcitabine and cisplatin only. Blood results or symptoms may change dates.

sections.title: Later visits
sections.text: Chemotherapy finishes after up to eight cycles. If treatment continues as planned, only durvalumab is given on day 1 of a 28-day cycle. Your team reviews benefit and side effects.

sections.title: Before leaving the unit
sections.text: Write down the next infusion, blood tests and the 24-hour oncology number. Ask which appointments change if a dose is delayed. Bring the wallet and passport to your next review.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: First-line treatment to slow advanced bile duct or gallbladder cancer and help people live longer.
evidence.population: Unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer
evidence.interpretation: The TOPAZ-1 trial compared adding durvalumab to gemcitabine and cisplatin with adding a placebo. At the three-year analysis, about 15 in 100 people in the durvalumab group and 7 in 100 in the placebo group were alive after three years.
evidence.limitations: These are results in selected trial groups. They cannot predict an individual response; ask how the findings apply to you.

teachback: Which medicines are given at your next visit, and which symptoms would make you phone today?
consent_support: Discuss the aim, alternatives including supportive care alone, possible benefit, immune effects that may be serious or permanent, possible need for steroids or long-term hormone treatment, and what matters most to the patient. Include infection, kidney, hearing and nerve risks from chemotherapy.

support.title: Carry the official immunotherapy alert card
support.text: Keep the card with you during treatment and afterwards. Show it to an out-of-hours doctor or emergency team and tell them when you last received immunotherapy.

support.title: If you become unwell
support.text: Use the 24-hour oncology number supplied by your hospital. If the team cannot be reached, seek urgent assessment. Follow the emergency action shown on your card.

support.title: Medicines and steroids
support.text: Show the team all prescription, over-the-counter and herbal medicines. Take prescribed steroids exactly as directed and ask before changing them.

support.title: During the chemotherapy phase
support.text: The unit gives fluids before cisplatin to help protect your kidneys. Your team will prescribe anti-sickness medicines and advise what to take at home. Ask about fluid intake if you have a heart or kidney condition.

support.title: During durvalumab maintenance
support.text: The chemotherapy medicines and their routine pre-infusion fluids finish. Bring your immunotherapy alert card and check your prescription for any continuing supportive medicine.

common_effects.title: Tiredness or low energy
common_effects.text: Rest when needed and tell your team if tiredness suddenly worsens.

common_effects.title: Nausea or loss of appetite
common_effects.text: Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines. Ask for help if eating or drinking becomes difficult.

common_effects.title: Low blood counts
common_effects.text: These may be found on blood tests. Report bruising or bleeding and call urgently for fever or shivering.

serious_effects.title: Lung inflammation (pneumonitis)
serious_effects.text: Contact oncology urgently for a new cough or breathlessness. Severe trouble breathing or chest pain needs 112 or 999.

serious_effects.title: Bowel inflammation (colitis)
serious_effects.text: Call oncology urgently for new diarrhoea, blood in stools or increasing abdominal pain.

serious_effects.title: Liver inflammation or bile drainage problems
serious_effects.text: Call urgently for yellow eyes or skin, dark urine or worsening upper abdominal pain.

serious_effects.title: Hormone problems
serious_effects.text: Unusual thirst, frequent urination, dizziness, vomiting, marked weakness or severe headache need urgent assessment. Collapse or confusion with severe illness needs emergency help.

serious_effects.title: Infection or blocked bile duct
serious_effects.text: Fever, shivering, jaundice or upper abdominal pain need urgent assessment, especially with a biliary stent.

serious_effects.title: Kidneys, hearing or nerves
serious_effects.text: Report much less urine, ringing in the ears, hearing changes or tingling promptly.

induction.title: Before the initial infusions
induction.text: Cisplatin is classified as having high vomiting risk. The unit prescribes prevention before treatment and tells you which medicines to take at home. Fluids before cisplatin protect your kidneys. Confirm your personal fluid plan.

induction.title: Between day 1 and day 8
induction.text: Bring your symptom and medicine record to day 8. Report hearing changes, reduced urine, vomiting despite prescribed medicine, fever or shaking chills promptly.

maintenance.title: When chemotherapy finishes
maintenance.text: Maintenance consists of durvalumab alone. Its vomiting risk is minimal. Your team reviews the prescription for anti-sickness medicines and fluids as you change phase.

maintenance.title: Immune symptoms can be delayed
maintenance.text: Carry the immunotherapy alert card during treatment and after it ends. Contact oncology urgently for a new cough, breathlessness, diarrhoea, jaundice or marked weakness.
